indicators.source: IMF, Unlocking the Potential: AI in Sub-Saharan Africa (Departmental Paper, 2026)
indicators.methodology: Complement of the source's low-exposure estimate: about four-fifths of jobs in sub-Saharan Africa have limited exposure to AI
indicators.note: Regional only. The source publishes no country split.

indicators.indicator: Illustrative AI workload as a share of a monthly wage benchmark
indicators.source: Computed from Synthetic frontier median benchmark (Across the retained frontier band) rate card and the country-specific wage benchmark
indicators.tier_label: Derived from academic and official inputs
indicators.methodology: An illustrative month of moderate use = 20 standard workloads at the synthetic median frontier workload price ($16.875 per workload), divided by the recorded monthly wage or documented country-specific monthly equivalent. Monthly equivalent of hourly rate using country-specific assumed hours.

indicators.indicator: Illustrative AI-use basket as a share of monthly GNI per capita
indicators.source: Computed from Synthetic frontier median benchmark rate card and World Bank GNI per-capita data
indicators.tier_label: Derived from reported pricing and official economic data
indicators.methodology: 20 standard workloads at the synthetic median frontier workload price ($16.875 per workload), divided by monthly GNI per capita on the Atlas method (annual value divided by 12). Published only when the latest non-empty GNI observation is within the five-calendar-year freshness window.
indicators.note: GNI per capita is a national-average economic indicator, not median earnings, household disposable income, or a typical worker's wage. The baseline rate card is trade-reported, so this derived comparison is not headline eligible.
